v01: Twenty Keynote slides, built one element at a time: eighty-one tool calls.
v02: M.C.P. Keynote builds the whole deck from one spec, in one call.
v03: Claude writes one spec: slides, tables, charts, notes and transitions.
v04: The server checks all of it before anything is created.
v05: A typo or an invented key comes back named, with what to use instead.
v06: Your text reaches Applescript as arguments, never pasted into the script,
v07: so a title full of quotes can't break it, or take it over.
v08: Then Keynote builds native tables with live formulas, seventeen chart types and styled connectors,
v09: and exports to P.D.F., PowerPoint, a movie or H.T.M.L.
v10: Describe deck reads an open deck back into the same spec, ready to diff in git.
v11: Seven hundred fifty-seven unit tests pass.
v12: On a real Keynote, two hundred eighty-nine live checks ran: none failed.
v13: It rebuilds By Axe's Keynote M.C.P., a fork of Easy Chen's original.
v14: M.C.P. Keynote. Keynote decks, built from one declarative spec.
